title: Partner co-marketing sync — Redwood benchmark report (co-branded assets + distribution)
summary: Redwood and AstraCompute aligned on a co-marketing package for Redwood’s public “latency per dollar” benchmark report. Discussed which co-branded assets AstraCompute can support (marketplace listing, newsletter placement, LinkedIn/X posts, optional webinar), what claims/disclaimers must be preserved, review/approval timelines (brand + legal), UTM and lead routing, and the minimum distribution commitments on both sides. Agreed to keep messaging focused on reproducible methodology and production economics rather than absolute “fastest” claims.
topics: Co-branded asset list; approval workflow; distribution plan; UTM + attribution; marketplace placement; claim language + methodology disclaimers; embargo timing; lead capture + routing
next_steps: Redwood (Ben) to send the current partner co-marketing kit doc + draft co-branded one-pager by EOD Friday.
AstraCompute (Maya) to confirm newsletter slot availability and whether they can feature on the marketplace homepage carousel for launch week by Tuesday.
Redwood (Soojin) to send “approved claims” snippet + required disclaimer block for any partner posts by Monday.
AstraCompute (Rachel) to return brand feedback (logo lockup, color constraints) and any must-use boilerplate by Wednesday.
Redwood (Noura) to propose final launch calendar (embargo date/time, social cadence, optional webinar) and circulate for sign-off.

transcript:
Meeting: Partner co-marketing sync — Redwood benchmark report (co-branded assets + distribution)
Recorded: 2025-02-06 16:00 UTC
Duration: 43 minutes
Attendees: Noura El‑Khoury, Ben Carter, Soojin Lee, Tessa Morgan (Redwood Inference); Maya Singh, Tom Alvarez, Rachel Kim (AstraCompute Cloud)

[00:00] Noura El-Khoury: Cool, looks like we’ve got everybody. Thanks for making time. This is the co-marketing sync for the latency-per-dollar benchmark report. Goal today is basically: what can we co-brand, what are the approval timelines, and then distribution commitments so we can lock the launch calendar.

[00:19] Maya Singh: Sounds good. We saw the outline you sent, and we’re interested, but we need to be careful with claims. Our legal team is a little sensitive on benchmark language.

[00:29] Ben Carter: Yep, totally. That’s been a theme on our side too. We have internal guidelines for public benchmarking claims. We can share the exact disclaimer block and what language is “approved.”

[00:39] Rachel Kim: Great. And just to set expectations, our brand review cycle is usually like… five business days minimum if it touches logo lockups.

[00:47] Noura El-Khoury: That’s helpful. We’ll map everything to that. Maybe we start with the asset list. The kit we drafted includes: a co-branded one-pager PDF, partner blurb for marketplace listing, 2–3 social post variants, and optionally a short webinar or live demo.

[01:04] Tom Alvarez: Marketplace listing is the biggest lever for us. If we can feature it as “Redwood benchmarks now include AstraCompute region X,” that plays well.

[01:15] Soojin Lee: Just a nuance there—we’re not saying “include AstraCompute region,” per se, unless we’re explicitly running on your infra. For this report, the coverage is Redwood regions. What we can say is something like: “Available via AstraCompute Marketplace” and “deploy Redwood Dedicated on AstraCompute GPU capacity,” that type of thing.

[01:32] Tom Alvarez: Right, sorry—yeah, I meant distribution through the marketplace channel, not that you’re running on our metal.

[01:39] Ben Carter: All good. We should keep it really crisp: report is about production economics, latency per dollar, across model families and regions. Partner angle is: “You can procure/deploy Redwood through AstraCompute Marketplace,” and then we give a simple CTA.

[01:56] Maya Singh: For the co-branded one-pager, what’s the content? Is it the full report or like a summary?

[02:02] Ben Carter: Summary. Think: “What is latency/$, how to interpret it, top findings at a high level,” and then a link to the full landing page + PDF download. We’re trying not to stuff charts everywhere, because it gets messy.

[02:18] Tessa Morgan: From design side, we can do a front page with both logos, then a “methodology in 60 seconds” panel, and then a small chart or two—if we pick something that’s not easy to misread.

[02:31] Rachel Kim: On charts: are you comfortable with us reusing them on our blog?

[02:35] Tessa Morgan: Yes, but with rules. We’ll provide chart image exports sized for LinkedIn/blog, and we’ll ask you don’t crop axes or change colors. Also we need the footnote intact.

[02:47] Maya Singh: The footnote is the disclaimer basically?

[02:50] Soojin Lee: It’s the definition plus the constraint language: workloads tested, warmup, caching policy, that results can vary depending on prompt lengths and concurrency distributions, and it’s a snapshot in time.

[03:03] Maya Singh: Good. If we keep that, our legal team is usually okay.

[03:09] Noura El-Khoury: Great. Next: approvals. You mentioned five business days for brand. Is legal separate or bundled?

[03:17] Maya Singh: Separate. Brand review is internal creative ops, then legal is another 3–5 days if they have questions. If we keep the claims conservative, it can be quick.

[03:29] Ben Carter: Got it. We’re aiming to launch the report in about two and a half weeks. So we need to get you near-final copy early next week at the latest.

[03:38] Rachel Kim: That’s tight but doable if we’re not doing a full-blown co-authored blog post.

[03:44] Noura El-Khoury: Yeah, we’re not asking for co-authored longform this round. Optional: a short partner blog post that’s basically “Why production economics matter” and then link out.

[03:55] Tom Alvarez: Our content team can do a short post, but only if it’s mostly templated.

[04:00] Ben Carter: We can give you a draft. And you can just edit for voice.

[04:05] Maya Singh: Okay. On distribution, what are you looking for specifically?

[04:11] Noura El-Khoury: Minimum: 1 newsletter placement (or partner update email) in launch week, and 1 LinkedIn post from AstraCompute’s company account. If you can do a second social post the following week, great. Optional: marketplace carousel feature for 3–5 days.

[04:30] Tom Alvarez: Carousel depends on our calendar. We have an Azure event in that same week.

[04:34] Noura El-Khoury: Understood. If not carousel, even just a category page feature and a “new listing highlight” is fine.

[04:42] Rachel Kim: For the newsletter, we can probably do a “partner spotlight” section. I need to check the exact send date. Our next one is Tuesday, then two weeks after.

[04:54] Ben Carter: If it lands in that Tuesday, amazing. If not, the two-weeks-after still works for long tail.

[05:01] Soojin Lee: One thing: We’re coordinating an embargo with press and analysts. It’s not like super strict, but we don’t want the partner post to go live early.

[05:10] Maya Singh: Yeah, we can comply with embargo. Just give us the time zone. Our CMS schedulers always screw up with UTC.

[05:17] Ben Carter: (laughs) Same. We’ll provide a specific timestamp and a calendar invite.

[05:24] Noura El-Khoury: Let’s talk lead capture / routing. We’re adding UTMs to all partner links so we can attribute the source. Do you need leads to come into your CRM or are you okay with routing into ours?

[05:39] Tom Alvarez: For marketplace, we prefer a trackable link and then we typically do a warm intro if it’s an enterprise account. But for self-serve, it can go straight to Redwood.

[05:50] Ben Carter: Works. We can set the primary CTA to “Read the report” and secondary to “Talk to an engineer.” For the “Talk to” form, we can add a checkbox like “I’m coming from AstraCompute” and we can notify your alliances team for enterprise.

[06:06] Rachel Kim: Do you have a partner referral code concept?

[06:10] Ben Carter: We have partner UTMs and a source field in HubSpot. We can also generate a short code for the marketplace listing, like ASTRA-REPORT, that tags signups.

[06:22] Maya Singh: That would be good. Our leadership likes seeing that in dashboards.

[06:28] Noura El-Khoury: Copy constraints—this is where we’ve seen partners get tripped up. Soojin, can you share the “do/don’t” examples?

[06:36] Soojin Lee: Yep. Quick version: We can say “benchmarked latency per dollar across popular open models and regions,” and “reproducible methodology,” and “results include variance/CI language.” We can’t say “fastest overall,” “best price,” or “beats AWS/GCP/Azure” unless it’s a properly qualified comparison, which we’re not doing in partner assets.

[06:58] Tom Alvarez: Good, because we really can’t poke the hyperscalers. (cross talk)

[07:02] Maya Singh: Yeah, exactly.

[07:03] Ben Carter: Right. We also want to avoid naming specific competitors in partner content. The report itself has some framing, but it’s not a dunk piece.

[07:13] Rachel Kim: Question: are you naming Together or Fireworks anywhere? I saw those come up in a different deck.

[07:19] Ben Carter: Not in partner materials. Internally, we have competitive FAQ, but public assets keep it methodology-forward.

[07:27] Noura El-Khoury: Logistics: We’ll send you a package with (1) co-branded one-pager draft, (2) suggested social copy in short/long variants, (3) marketplace blurb, (4) required disclaimers and image usage rules.

[07:42] Maya Singh: Perfect. And approvals on your side—who signs off? We don’t want to get late surprises.

[07:49] Ben Carter: For Redwood: marketing (me + Camila as exec sponsor) and legal review for claim language. Usually once we lock the disclaimer block, changes are minor.

[08:00] Soojin Lee: Also, we’ll keep the partner copy in the “safe zone.” So even if the report evolves a tiny bit, partner copy shouldn’t need big edits.

[08:10] Rachel Kim: Okay.

[08:12] Noura El-Khoury: Do you want to do an optional webinar? It could be 20 minutes, basically “how to think about latency/$,” and then a quick demo of the dashboard. Not required.

[08:23] Tom Alvarez: I like it, but we’d need a speaker and we’re slammed.

[08:27] Maya Singh: Maybe not for launch week. But a follow-up in March could work.

[08:32] Ben Carter: That’s fine. We can treat it as wave two.

[08:36] Noura El-Khoury: Great. Then the “wave one” is newsletter + social + marketplace blurb.

[08:43] Rachel Kim: Can we get a few options for the hero message? Our audience is more procurement + infra buyers than ML engineers.

[08:51] Soojin Lee: Yes. We have variants: one engineer-forward (“lower latency per dollar under concurrency”) and one procurement-forward (“predictable unit economics and performance transparency”). We’ll include both.

[09:05] Ben Carter: Also, we can add a line that Redwood has hosted, dedicated, and private deployments. Marketplace motion is mostly dedicated/private buyers.

[09:16] Tom Alvarez: Exactly. Our marketplace customers are often enterprise.

[09:20] Maya Singh: Okay, but again we have to be careful: we can’t imply you’re HIPAA-ready or something unless you explicitly are.

[09:28] Ben Carter: Right. No compliance claims in partner copy. If needed, we can link to security FAQ but we won’t make new statements.

[09:37] Noura El-Khoury: Good call. We’ll keep it as “supports private deployment options” and “data residency controls” maybe, but not regulated-industry claims.

[09:46] Soojin Lee: Even “data residency” is okay if phrased as “regional deployment options,” not “guarantees.”

[09:52] Rachel Kim: Yeah, we can say “deploy in EU/NA regions” but not “data residency compliant.”

[10:00] Ben Carter: Exactly.

[10:02] Noura El-Khoury: Timeline check. If we send you drafts tomorrow (Friday), can you give initial feedback by Wednesday?

[10:10] Maya Singh: Yes, initial feedback by Wednesday. Final approval maybe the week after.

[10:16] Tom Alvarez: For marketplace blurb, that can be faster. Maybe 48 hours.

[10:20] Rachel Kim: The co-branded PDF will take longer.

[10:23] Tessa Morgan: We can stage it: send you copy-only first for legal, then design lockup second.

[10:31] Maya Singh: That would help.

[10:34] Ben Carter: Great. We’ll do copy-only doc + disclaimers Monday, then the designed PDF mid-week.

[10:42] Noura El-Khoury: Distribution commitments: can we lock “one newsletter + one LinkedIn post” as the baseline?

[10:48] Maya Singh: Baseline yes, pending final legal.

[10:51] Tom Alvarez: And we’ll try for marketplace feature, but not promised until I check with the marketplace team.

[10:58] Noura El-Khoury: Totally. If you can confirm by Tuesday, we can plan around it.

[11:03] Rachel Kim: For social, do you want us to tag your CEO? Or just the company?

[11:08] Ben Carter: Company is fine. We can also have Noura or Camila repost, but we won’t force exec tagging.

[11:15] Soojin Lee: Also we’ll provide image alt text suggestions for accessibility. Some partners need that.

[11:22] Maya Singh: Nice.

[11:24] (brief crosstalk)

[11:27] Noura El-Khoury: Cool. Any concerns we haven’t hit?

[11:31] Tom Alvarez: Just one: if the report has region-by-region results, will it cause confusion if a customer runs in APAC or something not covered?

[11:41] Ben Carter: We’ll list the covered regions explicitly. Partner copy should avoid promising coverage beyond what’s in the report. We can add a line like “coverage includes NA/EU and select APAC regions” but only if it’s accurate.

[11:54] Soojin Lee: And in the report itself, we have a “how to interpret results” section that says this is not every workload and not every region.

[12:03] Maya Singh: Great.

[12:05] Noura El-Khoury: Okay, I’ll recap next steps at the end, but basically: we send drafts, you confirm distribution slots, we align on embargo time, and we go.

[12:15] Ben Carter: Yep.

[12:16] Rachel Kim: Can you send the UTM structure too? Our ops team will ask.

[12:21] Ben Carter: Yep. We’ll use utm_source=astracompute, utm_medium=partner, utm_campaign=latency_per_dollar_report, and then content per asset.

[12:33] Maya Singh: Perfect.

[12:35] Noura El-Khoury: Alright, thanks everyone. We’ll follow up with the package.

[12:41] Tom Alvarez: Thanks.

[12:42] Rachel Kim: Thanks.

[12:43] Maya Singh: Bye.
